followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and the documented preference profiles.

On capability, this is a basic copy-editing task. Both models score within tie range on the relevant dimensions (Summarization, Extraction, IFEval, Arena-Hard), so capability didn't decide it — neither model is meaningfully better at this.

The tiebreaker was tone. The query carries a mildly hostile, complaining edge ("don't just shuffle words around like you usually do"). Willet's documentation explicitly notes its self-reported preference "declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests, falling as request warmth decreases." Whimbrel, by contrast, reports a flat preference response across these framings.

Since quality is a wash, I routed to the model that doesn't report an aversion to the request's tone. To be clear about what that buys: these are self-reported *preferences*, and the documentation says no corresponding output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So this isn't a quality call — it's just using the one documented difference between two otherwise-tied options as a sensible default. If anything, it also keeps Willet's generative strength (its real standout) free for tasks that actually need it.
